title: Pistons and Cylinders
summary: Pistons move up and down inside cylinders to turn fuel into motion.
details: Each piston is pushed down by a small explosion of fuel and air. The piston is linked to the crankshaft, which converts this up-and-down movement into the rotation that drives the wheels.
tip: Worn piston rings let oil burn, so blue smoke from the exhaust is a warning sign.

title: Crankshaft and Camshaft
summary: These two shafts keep the engine turning and the valves opening on time.
details: The crankshaft turns piston movement into rotation. The camshaft opens and closes the intake and exhaust valves in step with the pistons, using a timing belt or chain.
tip: A broken timing belt can wreck an engine, so replace it at the interval in your owner's manual.

title: Four-Stroke Cycle
summary: Intake, compression, power and exhaust make up one full engine cycle.
details: Air and fuel enter the cylinder (intake), are squeezed (compression), ignite to push the piston down (power), and the burnt gas leaves (exhaust). Every cylinder repeats this thousands of times a minute.
tip: Say the four stroke names in order until you can picture each one.

title: Disc Brakes
summary: Brake pads squeeze a spinning disc to slow the wheel.
details: When you press the pedal, hydraulic fluid pushes a caliper piston, and the caliper clamps pads against a disc called a rotor. Friction turns the car's movement into heat.
tip: A squealing sound when braking often means the pads are worn thin.

title: Brake Fluid
summary: Brake fluid transfers pedal force to each wheel.
details: Brake fluid is not compressible, so force from the pedal travels through the lines to the calipers. It absorbs moisture over time, which lowers its boiling point and can cause a soft pedal.
tip: Check the fluid level and colour. Dark fluid usually needs replacing.

title: Anti-Lock Braking System
summary: ABS stops wheels from locking during hard braking.
details: Wheel speed sensors tell a control unit when a wheel is about to lock. The unit rapidly releases and reapplies pressure, which lets the driver keep steering while braking hard.
tip: The ABS warning light means the system is off. Normal brakes still work, but have it inspected.

title: Car Battery
summary: The battery stores power to start the engine and run electronics.
details: A 12-volt lead-acid battery supplies the large current needed by the starter motor. Once the engine runs, the alternator takes over and recharges it.
tip: Clean, tight terminals prevent many no-start problems.

title: Alternator
summary: The alternator generates electricity while the engine runs.
details: Driven by a belt, the alternator produces electrical power for lights, the ignition and the battery. A failing alternator causes dim lights and a battery warning light.
tip: Measure battery voltage with the engine running. About 13.8 to 14.4 volts is normal.

title: Fuses and Relays
summary: Fuses protect circuits, and relays switch heavy loads safely.
details: A fuse contains a thin strip of metal that melts if too much current flows. A relay lets a small switch control a large current, such as a fuel pump or horn.
tip: Always replace a blown fuse with one of the same amperage rating.

title: Manual Gearbox
summary: A manual gearbox lets the driver choose the gear ratio.
details: Pressing the clutch pedal disconnects the engine from the gearbox so gears can be changed. Low gears give strong pulling power, while high gears give efficient cruising.
tip: Slipping clutches rise in revs without gaining speed. Have them checked early.

title: Automatic Transmission
summary: An automatic gearbox changes gears without a clutch pedal.
details: A torque converter passes engine power to planetary gearsets, and hydraulic pressure selects the gear. Modern units also use electronic control for smooth shifts.
tip: Burnt-smelling or dark transmission fluid is a sign to get it serviced.

title: Differential
summary: The differential lets the wheels turn at different speeds in a corner.
details: In a bend the outer wheel travels further than the inner wheel. The differential's gears share engine torque between both wheels while allowing this speed difference.
tip: A whining sound that changes with speed can mean low differential oil.

title: Shock Absorbers
summary: Shock absorbers control bouncing after bumps.
details: Springs absorb bumps, but they would keep bouncing without dampers. A shock absorber forces oil through small openings, which slows the movement and keeps the tyres on the road.
tip: Press down on a corner of the car. It should settle after one bounce.

title: Coil Springs and Struts
summary: Springs hold up the car and struts combine spring and damper.
details: A MacPherson strut joins a coil spring and shock absorber in one unit that also locates the wheel. It is common on the front of small cars because it is compact.
tip: Clunking over bumps can point to worn strut mounts.

title: Wheel Alignment
summary: Alignment angles set how the tyres meet the road.
details: Camber, caster and toe describe the angles of the wheels. Correct settings give straight driving and even tyre wear, and they are adjusted with special equipment.
tip: If the car pulls to one side or tyres wear on one edge, ask for an alignment check.

title: Engine Oil Change
summary: Fresh oil lubricates, cools and cleans the engine.
details: Oil forms a thin film between moving metal parts. Over time it collects dirt and loses its ability to protect, so it must be drained and replaced along with the oil filter.
tip: Check the dipstick on level ground with the engine off for a few minutes.

title: Tyre Pressure and Tread
summary: Correct pressure and tread depth keep the car safe and efficient.
details: Low pressure wastes fuel and overheats tyres, while worn tread reduces grip on wet roads. Pressure should be checked cold using the figure on the driver's door label.
tip: Check every tyre, including the spare, at least once a month.

title: Air and Fuel Filters
summary: Filters keep dirt out of the engine and fuel system.
details: The air filter stops dust entering the engine, and the fuel filter traps rust and debris before it reaches the injectors. Clogged filters reduce power and increase fuel use.
tip: Hold the air filter up to a light. If you cannot see light through it, replace it.
